messages:
Ben (Sales): Heads up team — Aperture Analytics' sandbox import flaked with 429s and some downstream generate calls also started failing during the run. Big exec demo tomorrow at 10am PT. acct:APT-204. Need triage + a short customer note about billing/security.

Zoe (SE): Which endpoints exactly? Are the 429s on embeddings or /v1/generate or both? Any sample headers?

Ben (Sales): Primary issue on /v1/embeddings during the ingest, but we saw cascading 429s on /v1/generate when the app tried to post-process embeddings in parallel. Sample header: HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 140
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 2501239900
Body: {"error":"rate_limited","detail":"per_route_cap"}

Hector (Infra): Sounds like per-route buckets for both endpoints drained because they did a high-parallel pattern: ~60 workers doing single-item embedding calls and simultaneous generate calls after each item. Account-level usage had headroom but each route had a tighter short-window cap. Short-term: add per-route reservation on embeddings and generate, or throttle client.

Ben (Sales): Customer can't rewrite ingest before demo. Can we apply a temporary reservation that covers both routes for a short window? They also asked whether reservations will be charged and whether data stays in-region.

Rina (Oncall): I can apply a combined reservation: +220 rps on /v1/embeddings and +80 rps on /v1/generate for APT-204 for 4 hours. Will enable extra traces to confirm it's their parallelism causing the drain. Applying now.

quota-bot: Temporary reservations applied: +220 rps to "/v1/embeddings" and +80 rps to "/v1/generate" for acct:APT-204 until 2501243600. Ticket: POC-AP-9001. :white_check_mark:

Zoe (SE): For the customer I recommend: 1) batch embeddings (up to 64 items/call) to reduce QPS, 2) separate ingest and post-processing stages to avoid simultaneous bursts, 3) add exponential backoff on 429s. Quick pasteable retry snippet (js):
```js
for (let i=0;i<5;i++){
  try { await client.embeddings.create(batch); break }
  catch(e){ if (e.status===429) await sleep((2**i)*100 + Math.random()*50); else throw e }
}
```

June (Finance): Quick billing note to paste: temporary POC reservations are provided as a courtesy and not billed to the customer during the trial. We log usage for internal conversion analysis. If they want a persistent dedicated reservation, we'll include it in the contract.

Marta (Security): Security blurb: sandbox workloads run in the region selected at signup. For regulated data or stricter controls we offer Redwood Private with VPC, KMS/HSM, and audit trails. We can share SOC2 artifacts and a standard security questionnaire response.

Ben (Sales): Sending consolidated message to customer now. They also asked if per-item embeddings count toward token budgets differently — they worry their token budget will be exhausted alongside request quotas.

Hector (Infra): Clarify: embeddings are metered per-item and affect request-rate buckets; they may show low token volume yet consume high QPS if they do many single-item calls. Token budget and request-rate quotas are separate but both can be limiting. We'll add a short explanation to the POC runbook.

Zoe (SE): Follow-ups for internal: 1) update SE POC checklist to ask for expected concurrency and whether post-processing runs in parallel, 2) add a canned SE reply covering billing + security wording, 3) propose a small opt-in trial reservation option in the console. I'll open tickets for these.

Rina (Oncall): Demo run completed at 2501239988, no further 429s observed. I'll leave traces on until TTL and then revoke reservations.

Ben (Sales): Customer confirmed demo success and appreciated the quick support. I'll keep ticket POC-AP-9001 open for 24h for smoke checks. Thanks all! :rocket:
